Thought: Let me identify each compound from its SMILES notation:
- ClC1=CC=CC=C1: This is chlorobenzene (benzene with a chlorine substituent)
- O=[N+](C1=CC=CC=C1)[O-]: This is nitrobenzene (benzene with a nitro group)
- OC1=CC=CC=C1: This is phenol (benzene with a hydroxyl group)

In electrophilic aromatic substitution reactions, the reactivity depends on whether the substituent is activating or deactivating:
- Hydroxyl (-OH) is strongly activating (makes the ring more reactive)
- Chlorine (-Cl) is weakly deactivating (makes the ring less reactive)
- Nitro (-NO2) is strongly deactivating (makes the ring much less reactive)

So the order from most to least reactive would be:
1. Phenol (OC1=CC=CC=C1) - most reactive due to strong activating OH group
2. Chlorobenzene (ClC1=CC=CC=C1) - less reactive due to weakly deactivating Cl
3. Nitrobenzene (O=[N+](C1=CC=CC=C1)[O-]) - least reactive due to strongly deactivating NO2 group
